Feature: Visual-regression quality gate (strict mode + regression flags)
User Story: As a maintainer, my visual-regression run FAILS when a render comes out broken (empty, frozen, too short) or measurably worse than the baseline — not only when rendering crashes.
Expected Behavior: tools/visual_regression.py records per-render metrics (duration, fps, blank/static spans, subtitle cues) but previously only failed on render crashes: quality 'warn' cases and baseline deltas never affected the exit code. Adds pure, unit-tested gate logic: quality_failures(case) returns hard violations (duration<2s, fps<5, blank span>0.5s, dominant static span, a lesson with zero subtitle cues); compare_report flags regressions vs. a baseline run (duration collapse >25%, blank/static-ratio increases) with a regression_count; and decide_exit(report, strict) fails on render crashes always, and additionally on quality violations, soft warnings, and regressions under the new --strict flag. Default (non-strict) behavior is unchanged.
Notes: Verified: visual-regression quality gate: quality_failures + regression flags + strict exit (F162)
